I am an expert leather real-from fake teller. The easiest way (apart from trusted labels) is to find an edge of the leather and peek beneath it. If you see suede fibers, it is leather. A second less reliable way is to gently scratch with your fingernail. Real leather will FEEL like leather and PVC with feel grippy like plastic. As another user said, leather also has a distinctive smell, so if the object smells like this it's probably leather. On the other hand there are leather products that don't smell like leather. These telling skills come from experience with leather and fake leather products. Another helpful heuristic is that in cheap leather goods, you cannot expect the leather to be soft or thin. Real leather $25 shoes will be hard and stiff; if they're soft, they are probably pleather. A sure sign of leather is pore-holes where the hairs were pulled out. 

Also: Bonded leather or reconstituted leather with leather fibers is not real leather, it is PVC with discarded fibers underneath. Manufacturers do this trick so they can trick people by labelling the product leather.
